log.text: Toxic Spikes up on P2's side

decisions.rationale: Mega Charizard-Y leads with Drought to enable sun-boosted Heat Wave and Solar Beam, pressuring Metagross and Primarina. Volcarona threatens immediate damage with Heat Wave and can sweep late-game with Quiver Dance. Toxapex walls Primarina and sets Toxic Spikes, while Torkoal backs up Drought and disrupts with Yawn. This lineup balances immediate pressure, disruption, and late-game sweep potential.
decisions.notebook: Primary threats: Mega Metagross (Tough Claws Meteor Mash/Rock Slide), Farigiraf/Primarina Trick Room, and Sinistcha Rage Powder. Sun from Mega Charizard-Y or Torkoal is critical to boost Fire moves and enable Solar Beam, while Volcarona and Dragapult provide speed control and sweep potential. Toxapex and Arbok disrupt with Toxic Spikes and Intimidate/Glare, respectively. Plan to preserve Volcarona for late-game sweeps under sun, using Toxapex and Torkoal to stall and disrupt. Watch for opponent’s Trick Room and Rage Powder to adjust positioning and target priority.

decisions.rationale: Lead Farigiraf + Sinistcha: Armor Tail blocks Sucker Punch, Mental Herb stops Taunt, Heatproof Sinistcha takes neutral Fire and redirects with +2 Rage Powder while Farigiraf sets TR. Mega Metagross cleans sun abusers with Rock Slide (4x on Zard/Volc) and Tough Claws-boosted STAB. Primarina OHKOs Dragapult with Moonblast and pressures Toxapex with Psychic Noise. Conkeldurr and Overqwil sit for this game.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brings sun (Charizard-Y + Torkoal) with Volcarona abuse, fast Dragapult, bulky Toxapex, and Arbok Intimidate + Glare. My TR plan: Farigiraf + Sinistcha lead with Armor Tail + Heatproof + Rage Powder to guarantee TR. Mega Metagross is primary sweeper. Primarina answers Dragapult/Toxapex. Conkeldurr Wide Guard and Overqwil Intimidate are matchup-dependent alternates. Watch for Arbok Glare bypassing Mental Herb and double-target snipes on Farigiraf.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving Charizard-Y first turn secures sun immediately, boosting Fire moves and enabling Solar Beam later. Heat Wave pressures both foes, especially super-effective vs Sinistcha, while Volcarona’s Heat Wave adds damage. This line avoids Rage Powder redirection and minimizes risk from Trick Room or early Metagross threats. KOing Sinistcha early disrupts opponent’s redirection and spread damage plans.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize Mega Charizard-Y first turn to secure sun and pressure Sinistcha, the primary redirection threat. Volcarona’s Heat Wave complements damage output while preserving Protect for scouting. Avoid Solar Beam turn 1 due to Sinistcha’s resistance and Rage Powder risk. Watch for opponent’s Trick Room timing; if set, pivot to Toxapex or Torkoal to disrupt. Preserve Volcarona for late-game sweeps under sun, using Quiver Dance + Heat Wave/Bug Buzz. Toxapex and Torkoal serve as defensive pivots to absorb hits and disrupt with Toxic Spikes/Yawn. Metagross is the primary offensive threat; prioritize KOing it with Charizard’s Solar Beam or Volcarona’s Bug Buzz under sun.

decisions.rationale: Farigiraf sets TR after sun attackers have moved, so it will likely be KO'd by double Heat Wave. Switching it to Primarina preserves it while Sinistcha Protects to blank all damage. Primarina resists Fire, so it tanks spread hits; next turn we can pivot back to Farigiraf under safer conditions and attempt TR again.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brings sun (Charizard-Y, Torkoal, Volcarona) with fast Dragapult, bulky Toxapex, Arbok Intimidate/Glare. Our TR: Farigiraf + Sinistcha with Armor Tail + Heatproof + Rage Powder. Farigiraf vulnerable to double spread turn 1; switching to Primarina when facing double spread preserves TR setter. Mega Metagross is primary sweeper; Primarina answers Dragapult/Toxapex. Conkeldurr Wide Guard and Overqwil Intimidate are matchup-dependent alternates. Watch for Arbok Glare bypassing Mental Herb and double-target snipes on Farigiraf.

decisions.rationale: Primarina is 2HKOed by Solar Beam under sun and threatens Charizard with Moonblast. KOing it now removes the immediate Fairy-type threat and prevents a potential sweep. Volcarona Protect scouts opponent’s next move, preserving it for late-game Quiver Dance sweeps under sun. Sinistcha’s resistance to Grass and Rage Powder redirection make it a suboptimal Solar Beam target. Heat Wave is less urgent with Primarina at 48% and Sinistcha likely to Protect again.
decisions.notebook: Primarina is the primary immediate threat due to its Fairy typing and Moonblast’s super-effective damage on Charizard. KOing it turn 2 removes a key offensive pivot and simplifies the late-game. Volcarona’s Protect preserves it for sun-boosted Quiver Dance sweeps, especially if Trick Room is set. Sinistcha’s Rage Powder and resistance to Grass make it a lower-priority target; prioritize removing Primarina first. Watch for Metagross Mega Evolution timing; if it Mega Evolves, pivot to Toxapex or Torkoal to disrupt with Toxic Spikes or Yawn. Preserve Charizard’s Solar Beam for Metagross or Farigiraf if Primarina is already KOed.

decisions.rationale: Rage Powder at +2 redirects both attacks to Heatproof Sinistcha, blanking any Fire move aimed at the switch slot. Metagross enters for free and threatens both Char-Y (4x Rock) and Volcarona (2x Rock) next turn. If Sinistcha survives one Heat Wave, we have TR + Rock Slide pressure. If it faints, Farigiraf comes in to set TR with Armor Tail blocking Sucker Punch. Solar Beam into Metagross does only 15-33%, so even a hard read doesn't punish us.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Opponent brings sun (Charizard-Y, Torkoal, Volcarona) with fast Dragapult, bulky Toxapex, Arbok Intimidate/Glare. Our TR mode: Farigiraf + Sinistcha with Armor Tail + Heatproof + Rage Powder. Mega Metagross Rock Slide threatens both Char-Y (4x) and Volcarona (2x). Primarina answers Dragapult/Toxapex. Conkeldurr Wide Guard and Overqwil Intimidate are alternate options for later games. Watch for Arbok Glare bypassing Mental Herb and double-target snipes on Farigiraf. Sinistcha Heatproof crucial for surviving single Fire attacks in sun; still at risk from double Heat Wave.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Metagross Rock Slide threatens OHKO on Charizard; Solar Beam risks free turn if Metagross Protects. Flamethrower guarantees damage on Metagross, avoiding Solar Beam’s charge risk. Volcarona Protect avoids spread damage and preserves it for sun-boosted Quiver Dance sweeps. Primarina is already weakened; focus on Metagross to simplify late-game.
decisions.notebook: Primarina is the primary immediate threat due to Fairy typing and Moonblast’s super-effective damage on Charizard. KOing it turn 2 removed the key offensive pivot. Metagross Mega Evolution timing is critical; if it Mega Evolves, pivot to Toxapex or Torkoal to disrupt with Toxic Spikes or Yawn. Preserve Charizard’s Solar Beam for Farigiraf or Metagross if Primarina is already KOed. Volcarona’s Protect preserves it for sun-boosted Quiver Dance sweeps under sun. Sinistcha’s Rage Powder and resistance to Grass make it a lower-priority target unless Trick Room is set.

decisions.rationale: Torkoal maintains sun for offensive pressure and resists Rock Slide, while Toxapex absorbs Rock Slide and sets Toxic Spikes. This split balances offense and defense, disrupting Metagross and preparing for Trick Room.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Mega Evolution is confirmed; prioritize resisting Rock Slide and maintaining sun. Toxapex’s Toxic Spikes are valuable for passive damage, but Torkoal’s sun and Yawn are critical for disrupting Trick Room. Primarina remains a key threat under Trick Room due to Moonblast. Preserve Toxapex for late-game defensive utility and Torkoal for sun-based offense.

decisions.rationale: Double Heat Wave is the opponent's obvious best play. Sinistcha Protect hard-blocks it while Megagross Rock Slide punishes: 77-145% into Char-Y and 82-159% into Volcarona (4x both). If they deviate with single-target moves, Protect still absorbs one and Metagross fires. Mega for the ~3-5% extra damage edge. Worst case: they double Protect, we burn a turn but keep both healthy.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 vs sun (Char-Y/Torkoal/Volcarona/Dragapult/Toxapex/Arbok). Farigiraf+Sinistcha TR mode: Armor Tail blocks priority snipes, Heatproof critical for surviving single Fire attacks in sun but double Heat Wave still overwhelms. Mega Metagross Rock Slide is our primary anti-sun breaker with 4x on both Char-Y and Volcarona. Primarina eats Fire hits well (Water resist). Opponent likes double spread and Protect cycling with Volcarona. Arbok Intimidate+Glare threatens physical attackers; Mental Herb Farigiraf blocks one Glare.

decisions.rationale: Protect stalls Metagross Rock Slide (~28% max) while Toxic Spikes punishes switches. Sun remains active, forcing Sinistcha to either Protect (wasting a turn) or eat Toxic Spikes. Metagross cannot OHKO Torkoal, and Toxapex avoids Haze/Trick Room disruption. Primarina threat is mitigated by sun and Toxapex’s bulk.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Rock Slide is non-OHKO under sun; prioritize Protect to stall. Toxic Spikes are critical for passive damage, especially against Primarina. Sinistcha’s Rage Powder is less threatening with Volcarona/Charizard gone; Torkoal’s Yawn can disrupt Trick Room if Toxapex is preserved. Preserve Toxapex’s Recover for late-game under Trick Room. Sun is the win condition—avoid Heat Wave unless both foes are locked into attacks.

decisions.rationale: Heat Wave spread threatens OHKO on Sinistcha and huge damage on Metagross. Double switching to resists (Primarina) and full HP (Farigiraf) preserves our mega and resets Sinistcha’s shaky Protect success. We can set Trick Room with Farigiraf next turn and bring Metagross back after sun expires.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 sun mode (Char-Y/Torkoal/Volcarona). Torkoal set: Heat Wave, Body Press, Yawn, Protect (Bold, Heat Rock). Toxapex set: Muddy Water, Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover (Calm, Leftovers). Opponent cycles double spread and Protect. Our Primarina lacks Water STAB (Moonblast/Psychic Noise/Icy Wind/Protect). Farigiraf is our secondary TR setter; Armor Tail blocks priority snipes. Plan: preserve Metagross-Mega for midgame under Trick Room; apply Psychic pressure to Toxapex with Primarina/Farigiraf; set TR when safe.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Protect stalls sun for 1 more turn, forcing foes to attack or waste turns. Muddy Water pressures both foes, especially Farigiraf (Toxic Spikes synergy). Recover is unnecessary at full HP. Yawn risks Toxapex eating Psychic Noise unprotected.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Rock Slide is non-OHKO under sun but chips Torkoal heavily; prioritize Protect to stall. Toxic Spikes are critical for passive damage, especially against Primarina. Sinistcha’s Rage Powder is less threatening without Charizard/Volcarona; Torkoal’s Yawn can disrupt Trick Room if Toxapex is preserved. Sun is the win condition—avoid Heat Wave unless both foes are locked into attacks. Preserve Toxapex’s Recover for late-game under Trick Room.

selection: Trick Room (all adjacent, including ally Primarina)
decisions.rationale: Protect blocks Yawn/Heat Wave on Primarina; Farigiraf sets TR safely, surviving Heat Wave (29-44%). Sun ends after turn; Metagross cleans under TR without fearing sun-boosted Fire. Mental Herb blocks Taunt, Yawn accepted—switch Farigiraf out if slept. Minimises risk while securing win condition.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s Torkoal has Yawn (bold, Heat Rock). Toxapex uses Recover and Haze. Toxic Spikes on our field limits switch-ins. Metagross-Mega is our midgame TR sweeper. Sinistcha has Rage Powder for redirection. Opponent likely to stall and spread damage; we must set TR and eliminate Toxapex first to prevent Recover loops.

decisions.rationale: Primarina Protect + Farigiraf Psychic threatens Toxapex OHKO. Protect stalls Trick Room, Recover preserves Toxapex for Toxic Spikes and late-game. Sun and passive damage are win conditions; avoid Heat Wave unless both foes are locked into attacks.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Rock Slide is non-OHKO under sun but chips Torkoal heavily; prioritize Protect to stall. Toxic Spikes are critical for passive damage, especially against Primarina. Sinistcha’s Rage Powder is neutralized; Torkoal’s Yawn can disrupt Trick Room if Toxapex is preserved. Sun is the win condition—avoid Heat Wave unless both foes are locked into attacks. Preserve Toxapex’s Recover for late-game under Trick Room. Farigiraf Psychic is a 2x OHKO risk; Protect first to scout and stall.

decisions.rationale: Double Psychic into Toxapex gives 86.6–150.4% combined range with heal block from Psychic Noise. Removing Toxapex eliminates Recover stall and leaves Torkoal alone. Torkoal's Heat Wave does only 7–13.5% to Primarina; Yawn is the bigger threat but worth risking for the KO. TR has 4 turns left—clearing Toxapex now lets Metagross clean up.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Torkoal: Yawn, Heat Wave, Body Press, Protect (Heat Rock, Bold). Toxapex: Muddy Water, Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover (Leftovers, Calm, Regenerator). Toxic Spikes on our field limits switch-ins. Metagross-Mega is TR sweeper; Sinistcha has Rage Powder redirection. Priority: eliminate Toxapex to prevent Recover loops, then handle Torkoal. Opponent tends to Protect and spread damage.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Toxapex is one Psychic from death under Heal Block. Haze clears Heal Block, enabling Recover next turn to survive. Protect Torkoal to scout and stall for sun. Yawn is slower and risks Farigiraf Psychic first.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Rock Slide is non-OHKO under sun but chips Torkoal heavily; prioritize Protect to stall. Toxic Spikes are critical for passive damage, especially against Primarina. Sinistcha’s Rage Powder is neutralized; Torkoal’s Yawn can disrupt Trick Room if Toxapex is preserved. Sun is the win condition—avoid Heat Wave unless both foes are locked into attacks. Preserve Toxapex’s Recover for late-game under Trick Room. Farigiraf Psychic is a 2x OHKO risk; Haze is the only way to clear Heal Block and enable Recover. Primarina’s Psychic Noise is also a 2x OHKO under Heal Block.

decisions.rationale: Psychic Noise guarantees Toxapex KO at 2% (Heal Blocked, no Recover). Farigiraf Psychic is the strongest single-target into Torkoal (31-61%). Removing Toxapex leaves only Torkoal — opponent has no remaining bench. Speed tie under TR is irrelevant; both lines resolve favorably regardless of order. Hyper Voice spread is weaker and unnecessary with Toxapex already KO'd.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Torkoal: Yawn, Heat Wave, Body Press, Protect (Heat Rock, Bold). Toxapex: Muddy Water, Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover (Leftovers, Calm, Regenerator). Toxic Spikes on our field limits switch-ins. Metagross-Mega is TR sweeper; Sinistcha has Rage Powder redirection. Priority: eliminate Toxapex to prevent Recover loops, then handle Torkoal. Opponent tends to Protect and spread damage. Dragapult and Arbok not brought G1.

decisions.rationale: Protect is safest to stall Trick Room and scout Metagross's move. Yawn is risky due to Rage Powder redirecting to Sinistcha, leaving Torkoal vulnerable to Psychic OHKO. Preserving Torkoal's HP is critical for sun win condition.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Rock Slide is a consistent 20-27% chip under neutral conditions, but sun reduces its power. Primarina's Icy Wind is negligible (6-9%) but Psychic Noise/Heal Block remains a 2x OHKO threat. Farigiraf's Psychic is the primary OHKO risk; Protect is mandatory to avoid it. Sinistcha's Rage Powder is neutralized by Heatproof, but Yawn may still be redirected. Toxic Spikes are critical for passive damage; prioritize preserving Torkoal to set sun and stall. Trick Room expires in 2 turns; focus on disrupting renewal while minimizing risk.

decisions.rationale: Double Psychic into Torkoal guarantees the KO (min 64.9% > 58% HP). Heat Wave cannot KO either mon. Yawn doesn't prevent our attacks this turn. Protect odds negligible after 4 consecutive uses. Simplest and safest path to close game 1.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Torkoal: Heat Wave, Body Press, Yawn, Protect (Heat Rock, Bold, Drought). Toxapex: Muddy Water, Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover (Leftovers, Calm, Regenerator). Torkoal used Protect 4 consecutive turns—future Protects near-impossible. Dragapult/Arbok not brought G1.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Primarina and Farigiraf both threaten OHKO with Psychic Noise/Psychic. Protect avoids this while preserving Torkoal for sun/stalwart. Yawn is risky under Trick Room; scouting is safer.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Rock Slide is consistent chip but sun mitigates it. Primarina's Psychic Noise/Heal Block is a 2x OHKO; Farigiraf's Psychic is the primary OHKO risk. Toxic Spikes are critical for passive damage; prioritize Torkoal preservation. Trick Room expires in 1 turn; disrupt renewal only if safe. Sinistcha's Rage Powder is neutralized by Heatproof, but Yawn may still target Torkoal. Endgame plan: stall with sun + Toxic Spikes, avoid unnecessary chip.

decisions.rationale: Combined minimum damage 64.9% exceeds Torkoal's 58% HP, guaranteeing KO regardless of speed tie or Torkoal's move. Psychic Noise outdamages Moonblast (neutral vs resisted). No need to reset Trick Room with only Torkoal remaining.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Torkoal: Heat Wave, Body Press, Yawn, Protect (Heat Rock, Bold, Drought). Used Protect 5 times — future success rate extremely low. Toxapex: Muddy Water, Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover (Leftovers, Calm, Regenerator). Dragapult/Arbok not brought G1.

reflections.summary: Team-preview plan was flawed: sun core (Charizard-Y + Torkoal) was overloaded by Primarina + Farigiraf's Psychic Noise/Heal Block under Trick Room, while Toxapex's Toxic Spikes were removed by Haze and passive damage was insufficient to offset the opponent's sustain (Primarina's Life Orb recovery, Farigiraf's bulk). Mega Metagross's Rock Slide chip compounded the problem by pressuring Torkoal into repeated Protects, preventing meaningful offensive presence.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Toxapex with a Trick Room setter (e.g., Indeedee-F) to enable self-sufficient Trick Room control and disrupt opponent's Psychic spam. Prioritize bringing a counter to Primarina (e.g., Amoonguss) to mitigate Heal Block and Psychic Noise pressure.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Primarina + Farigiraf Psychic spam under Trick Room is the primary wincon; Heal Block + Life Orb sustain is durable. Mega Metagross's Rock Slide is consistent chip (~15-20% per hit). Sinistcha's Rage Powder is situational but may pivot to Farigiraf. Future plans: Avoid sun core if opponent brings Primarina + Farigiraf; test Trick Room setter to flip field control. Target Primarina early to remove Heal Block threat.

reflections.summary: The opponent's sun team lacked Trick Room counters and Taunt, allowing Farigiraf to set Trick Room safely. Under Trick Room, Primarina and Farigiraf's Psychic-type moves overwhelmed Toxapex and Torkoal, while Heal Block prevented recovery. The opponent's overuse of Protect on Torkoal led to predictable failures, and their Toxapex was unable to stall effectively.
reflections.adjustment: Expect the opponent to bring Dragapult or Arbok next game to pressure Trick Room setters. Lead with Farigiraf and Primarina to maintain special offense and avoid Intimidate on Metagross. Preserve Metagross for late-game cleaning if Arbok is absent. Continue to exploit the lack of Taunt and prioritize removing Toxapex early to prevent Toxic Spikes accumulation.
reflections.notebook: Opponent Torkoal: Heat Wave, Body Press, Yawn, Protect (Heat Rock, Bold, Drought). Used Protect 5 times — future success rate extremely low. Toxapex: Muddy Water, Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover (Leftovers, Calm, Regenerator). Charizard-Mega-Y: Heat Wave, Solar Beam, Protect, Flamethrower (Timid). Volcarona: Quiver Dance, Heat Wave, Bug Buzz, Protect (Sitrus Berry, Flame Body, Timid). Dragapult: Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, U-turn, Dragon Dance (Life Orb, Infiltrator, Timid). Arbok: Gunk Shot, Sucker Punch, Glare, Protect (Expert Belt, Intimidate, Jolly). Opponent's team lacks Taunt; heavily Fire-weak to Rock/Water. Torkoal Protect overuse pattern noted. Toxapex Haze used but not impactful. Expect Dragapult or Arbok in G2. Plan: maintain Trick Room, prioritize special attackers to avoid Intimidate, eliminate Toxapex early. Armor Tail blocks Sucker Punch.
